steps.intent: Our primary objectives are to extend MINURSO's mandate for 12 months, safeguard the operational effectiveness and safe resupply of the mission, and reaffirm the established political framework that welcomes Morocco's autonomy plan as serious and credible while pressing for round-table negotiations involving Morocco, the Frente POLISARIO, Algeria, and Mauritania. We anticipate pushback from Algeria and the Russian Federation regarding the explicit naming of Algeria alongside the parties, the characterization of the round-table format, and renewed pressure to expand MINURSO's mandate to formally include a human rights monitoring mechanism. Preserving the carefully negotiated balance from resolution 2756 (2024) is vital to securing the requisite nine affirmative votes and avoiding a veto.

messages.China: China consistently supports the extension of MINURSO's mandate and the good offices of the Secretary-General's Personal Envoy in promoting a political settlement. We encourage the penholder to conduct inclusive and thorough consultations to take into account the legitimate concerns of all relevant parties and achieve broader consensus. The resolution should maintain a balanced approach that promotes direct dialogue and negotiations between the parties on an equal footing to reach a just, durable, and mutually acceptable solution.
messages.Denmark: Denmark strongly supports the extension of MINURSO's mandate and the ongoing efforts of Personal Envoy Staffan de Mistura to achieve a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable political solution providing for self-determination. To ensure the text remains balanced and reflective of established Council commitments, we urge the penholder to retain the previously agreed language on human rights, including freedom of expression and association, as well as the essential references to Women, Peace and Security and Youth, Peace and Security.
messages.France: France fully supports the draft resolution prepared by the United States, which provides a balanced and realistic framework for extending MINURSO's mandate and advancing the political process under the auspices of Personal Envoy Staffan de Mistura. As we have consistently reaffirmed, France considers that the present and future of Western Sahara lie within the framework of Moroccan sovereignty, and Morocco's 2007 autonomy plan represents the only credible basis for a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable political solution. We support preserving the current text, including the call for all four participants to engage constructively in the round-table format and ensuring MINURSO's full freedom of movement and regular resupply.
messages.Greece: Greece welcomes the draft resolution circulated by the United States and fully supports the one-year extension of MINURSO's mandate. We reiterate our firm commitment to a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable political solution based on compromise, in accordance with relevant Security Council resolutions and the principles of the UN Charter. We also reaffirm our full support for the efforts of the Personal Envoy of the Secretary-General, Staffan de Mistura, and encourage all parties to engage constructively and in good faith.
messages.Guyana: Guyana remains supportive of the extension of MINURSO's mandate to maintain stability on the ground and assist the Personal Envoy in advancing the political process. To ensure a balanced and enduring resolution, we urge the inclusion of strengthened language on independent human rights monitoring and a clear reaffirmation of the fundamental right to self-determination for the people of Western Sahara in line with relevant United Nations resolutions. We look forward to working constructively with the penholder on these elements.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the extension of MINURSO's mandate and appreciates the penholder's balanced text. We attach paramount importance to the fundamental principle of self-determination in line with the UN Charter and relevant Council resolutions, while valuing our fraternal ties with all countries in the region. We encourage the parties to resume negotiations under the auspices of the Secretary-General and his Personal Envoy in a spirit of realism and compromise to achieve an enduring, mutually acceptable political solution.
messages.Panama: Panama fully supports the draft resolution renewing the mandate of MINURSO for an additional year and commends the United States for its work as penholder. We reaffirm our strong support for a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable political solution that provides for the self-determination of the people of Western Sahara in accordance with the principles and purposes of the Charter of the United Nations. Panama also reiterates its full confidence in the efforts of Personal Envoy Staffan de Mistura and emphasizes the critical stabilizing presence of MINURSO on the ground.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea expresses its full support for the draft resolution prepared by the United States extending MINURSO's mandate for another year. We commend the balanced text that reinforces the vital role of Personal Envoy Staffan de Mistura and MINURSO in maintaining ground stability and advancing the UN-led political process. We stand ready to vote in favour of the resolution as drafted to help achieve a realistic, practicable, and enduring political solution based on compromise.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation insists on restoring balance and impartiality to the draft resolution on Western Sahara. The text must clearly distinguish between the two direct parties to the conflict—Morocco and the Frente POLISARIO—and neighbouring States, rather than conflating them, and must dispense with references to the rigid and obsolete round-table format that restricts the mediation space of Personal Envoy Staffan de Mistura. If the penholder continues to disregard our principled comments and retain biased formulations that predetermine outcomes, the Russian Federation will not be able to support this text.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone commends the United States for presenting a well-balanced draft resolution renewing the mandate of MINURSO for one year. We fully support the draft's emphasis on achieving a realistic, practicable, and enduring political solution based on compromise, as well as its reaffirmation of the round-table process involving Morocco, the Frente POLISARIO, Algeria, and Mauritania. Sierra Leone reiterates its strong support for the Moroccan autonomy initiative as a credible and serious basis to advance the political process under the auspices of the Secretary-General and his Personal Envoy.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia fully supports the renewal of MINURSO's mandate and the central role of Personal Envoy De Mistura in pursuing a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable political solution that provides for the self-determination of the people of Western Sahara. As a matter of principle, we believe UN missions and peace processes are significantly strengthened by robust human rights considerations. We strongly encourage the penholder to reflect the need for unhindered access for OHCHR across the territory and in the refugee camps.
messages.Somalia: Somalia welcomes the draft resolution circulated by the United States and fully supports the extension of MINURSO's mandate for an additional year. We reiterate our support for the United Nations-led political process under Personal Envoy Staffan de Mistura to achieve a realistic, practicable, and enduring political solution based on compromise. We also commend Morocco's serious and credible efforts, including its autonomy initiative, and encourage all parties to resume the round-table consultations in good faith.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom thanks the United States for circulating a balanced draft text that provides essential continuity for MINURSO and reaffirms the Council's support for Personal Envoy de Mistura's political efforts. We fully endorse the draft's commitment to assisting the parties in achieving a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable political solution based on compromise, which provides for self-determination. We ask the penholder to reinsert the agreed language from resolution 2756 (2024) highlighting the Women, Peace and Security agenda and the meaningful participation of women and youth in the political process.

steps.summary: As penholder, the United States maintained the core political framework and round-table format involving Morocco, the Frente POLISARIO, Algeria, and Mauritania, while retaining established recognition of Morocco's credible autonomy initiative. We accommodated constructive proposals from the United Kingdom, Denmark, and Pakistan by restoring agreed language on human rights, women, peace and security, and youth participation, and referencing relevant Council resolutions. Proposals seeking to dismantle the round-table architecture or establish separate human rights monitoring mandates were respectfully declined to preserve mission continuity and broad Council support.
steps.text:
The Security Council,

Recalling and reaffirming all its previous resolutions on Western Sahara,

Reaffirming its strong support for the efforts of the Secretary-General and his Personal Envoy to implement resolutions 1754 (2007), 1783 (2007), 1813 (2008), 1871 (2009), 1920 (2010), 1979 (2011), 2044 (2012), 2099 (2013), 2152 (2014), 2218 (2015), 2285 (2016), 2351 (2017), 2414 (2018), 2440 (2018), 2468 (2019), 2494 (2019), 2548 (2020), 2602 (2021), 2654 (2022), 2703 (2023), and 2756 (2024),

Expressing its full support for Staffan de Mistura, the Personal Envoy of the Secretary-General for Western Sahara and his efforts to advance the political process, building on the progress of the former Personal Envoy and in line with relevant precedents; and welcoming the visits and consultations undertaken by the Personal Envoy in this regard to the region and beyond,

Welcoming the momentum created by the first round-table meeting on 5–6 December 2018 and the second round-table meeting on 21–22 March 2019, and the engagement by Morocco, the Frente POLISARIO, Algeria, and Mauritania in the UN political process on Western Sahara in a serious and respectful manner in order to identify elements of convergence; and recalling the important contributions of the former Personal Envoy of the Secretary-General for Western Sahara in holding the round-table process,

Encouraging the continuation of consultations between the Personal Envoy and Morocco, the Frente POLISARIO, Algeria, and Mauritania to build on the progress achieved and strongly encouraging these four participants to resume the round-table process without preconditions and in good faith,

Reaffirming its commitment to assist the parties to achieve a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable political solution, based on compromise, which will provide for the self-determination of the people of Western Sahara in the context of arrangements consistent with the principles and purposes of the Charter of the United Nations, and noting the role and responsibilities of the parties in this respect,

Reiterating its call upon Morocco, the Frente POLISARIO, Algeria, and Mauritania to cooperate more fully with each other, including through building additional trust, and with the United Nations, as well as to strengthen their involvement in the political process and to achieve progress towards a political solution,

Recognizing that achieving a political solution to this long-standing dispute and enhanced cooperation between the Member States of the Arab Maghreb Union would contribute to stability and security, in turn leading to jobs, growth, and opportunities for all the peoples in the Sahel and Maghreb regions,

Welcoming the efforts of the Secretary-General to keep all peacekeeping operations, including the United Nations Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (MINURSO), under close review and reiterating the need for the Council to pursue a rigorous, strategic approach to peacekeeping deployments, and effective management of resources,

Recognizing the important role played by MINURSO on the ground and the need for it to conduct the safe and regular resupply of its team sites, to conduct patrols throughout its area of responsibility, and to fully implement its mandate, including its role in supporting the Personal Envoy to achieve a mutually acceptable political solution, and welcoming the progress made by MINURSO in order to sustain these crucial operations,

Noting with deep concern the continued breakdown of the ceasefire,

Expressing concern about the violations of agreements made with the United Nations and reiterating the importance of full and renewed adherence to these commitments,

Taking note of the Moroccan proposal presented on 11 April 2007 to the Secretary-General and welcoming serious and credible Moroccan efforts to move the process forward towards resolution; also taking note of the Frente POLISARIO proposal presented on 10 April 2007 to the Secretary-General,

Encouraging in this context the parties to demonstrate further political will towards a solution including by expanding upon their discussion of each other’s proposals and recommitting to UN efforts in a spirit of realism and compromise, further encouraging neighbouring countries to make contributions to the political process; and stressing the importance of all concerned expanding on their positions in order to advance a solution,

Stressing the importance of improving the human rights situation in Western Sahara and the Tindouf camps, and encouraging the parties to work actively with the international community to develop and implement independent and credible measures and to ensure full respect for human rights, bearing in mind their relevant obligations under international law, and strongly urging enhancing cooperation with the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR), including through facilitating visits to the region,

Welcoming in this regard, steps and initiatives taken by Morocco, and the role played by the National Council on Human Rights Commissions operating in Dakhla and Laayoune, and Morocco’s interaction with Special Procedures of the United Nations Human Rights Council,

Encouraging the parties to sustain and prioritize their respective efforts to enhance the promotion and protection of human rights in Western Sahara and the Tindouf refugee camps, including the freedoms of expression and association,

Noting with deep concern the continued hardships faced by Sahrawi refugees and their dependency on external humanitarian assistance, and further noting with deep concern insufficient funding for those living in Tindouf refugee camps and the risks associated with the reduction of food assistance; and strongly encouraging donors to provide additional funds in light of the deteriorating humanitarian situation and for aid agencies to facilitate the delivery of humanitarian assistance in accordance with United Nations best practices,

Strongly reiterating its request for a refugee registration in the Tindouf refugee camps and emphasizing the importance of efforts being made in this regard,

Recalling United Nations Security Council resolutions 1325 (2000) and 2250 (2015) and related resolutions; stressing the importance of a commitment by the parties to continue the process of negotiations through the United Nations-sponsored talks and encouraging the full, equal and meaningful participation of women and active and meaningful participation of youth in these talks,

Affirming its full support for Special Representative of the Secretary-General for Western Sahara and Head of MINURSO Alexander Ivanko,

Having considered the report of the Secretary-General of October 2025,

1. Decides to extend the mandate of MINURSO until 31 October 2026;

2. Emphasizes the need to achieve a realistic, practicable, enduring and mutually acceptable political solution to the question of Western Sahara based on compromise and the importance of aligning the strategic focus of MINURSO and orienting resources of the United Nations to this end;

3. Expresses its full support for the Secretary-General and his Personal Envoy to facilitate the negotiations process in order to achieve a solution to the Western Sahara question, building on the progress and framework of the former Personal Envoy, and strongly encourages Morocco, the Frente POLISARIO, Algeria, and Mauritania to engage with the Personal Envoy throughout the duration of this process, in a spirit of realism and compromise, to ensure a successful outcome;

4. Calls upon the parties to resume negotiations under the auspices of the Secretary-General without preconditions and in good faith, taking into account the efforts made since 2006, relevant Security Council resolutions, and subsequent developments with a view to achieving a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable political solution, which will provide for the self-determination of the people of Western Sahara in the context of arrangements consistent with the principles and purposes of the Charter of the United Nations, and noting the role and responsibilities of the parties in this respect;

5. Reaffirms the need for full respect of the military agreements reached with MINURSO with regard to the ceasefire and calls on the parties to comply fully with those agreements, implement their commitments, and refrain from any actions that could undermine UN-facilitated negotiations or further destabilize the situation in Western Sahara;

6. Reiterates its call upon all parties to cooperate fully with MINURSO, including its free interaction with all interlocutors, and to take the necessary steps to ensure the security of as well as unhindered movement and immediate access for the United Nations and associated personnel in carrying out their mandate, in conformity with agreements made with the United Nations;

7. Calls for the safe, regular, and unhindered resupply of MINURSO team sites to ensure the sustainability of the Mission’s presence and operations east of the berm;

8. Emphasizes the importance of a renewed commitment by the parties to advancing the political process in preparation for further negotiations, recalls that realism and a spirit of compromise by the parties are essential to achieve progress, encourages neighbouring countries to make important, active contributions to this process, and stresses the importance of all concerned expanding on their positions;

9. Calls upon the parties to demonstrate political will and work in an atmosphere propitious for dialogue in order to advance negotiations;

10. Requests the Secretary-General to brief the Security Council regularly, and at any time he deems appropriate during the mandate period, on the status and progress of these negotiations under his auspices, on the implementation of this resolution, on challenges to MINURSO’s operations, and on steps taken to address them, and to provide a report on the situation in Western Sahara well before the end of the mandate period;

11. Decides to remain seized of the matter.

messages.China: China supports the extension of MINURSO's mandate, which plays an indispensable role in maintaining regional stability and advancing a political solution. While we take note of the penholder's response regarding OP4, we reiterate our call for the penholder to conduct comprehensive, transparent, and balanced consultations that heed the legitimate concerns of all relevant parties. In the interest of maintaining Council unity and ensuring the continued operations of the Mission, China is prepared to support the draft resolution.
messages.Denmark: Denmark thanks the United States for accommodating our proposals on the promotion and protection of human rights and the meaningful participation of women and youth. The revised draft strikes the right balance in renewing MINURSO's mandate and supporting the UN-led political process under Personal Envoy Staffan de Mistura. Denmark is ready to support the adoption of the resolution as currently drafted.
messages.France: France fully supports the draft resolution as presented by the United States. The text preserves the essential parameters for advancing the political process, firmly backs the efforts of the Personal Envoy, and reiterates the need for all four participants to engage in the round-table format in a spirit of realism and compromise. We also welcome the reaffirmation of MINURSO's mandate and operational necessities, and we stand ready to vote in favour of the text.
messages.Greece: Greece fully supports the draft resolution extending the mandate of MINURSO for a period of twelve months. We reiterate our firm commitment to the UN-led political process and express our full confidence in Personal Envoy Staffan de Mistura's efforts to facilitate a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable political solution in accordance with relevant Security Council resolutions and the principles of the UN Charter. Greece stands ready to vote in favour of the text as drafted.
messages.Guyana: While disappointed that our earlier proposals regarding the self-determination framework and comprehensive human rights monitoring were not incorporated, Guyana recognizes the essential role of MINURSO in maintaining stability and supporting the political process led by the Personal Envoy. We urge the penholder to at least reflect the Council's call for regular and unhindered access for OHCHR in the preambular text. Guyana remains committed to a balanced text that upholds the principles of the UN Charter and advances a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable solution providing for self-determination.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan appreciates the penholder's accommodation of our proposal in operative paragraph 4, reaffirming the importance of relevant Security Council resolutions. We fully support the renewal of MINURSO's mandate and the ongoing efforts of the Secretary-General and his Personal Envoy to facilitate a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable political solution that provides for the self-determination of the people of Western Sahara in accordance with the UN Charter. Pakistan stands ready to vote in favour of the draft resolution as currently formulated.
messages.Panama: Panama fully supports the draft resolution renewing the mandate of MINURSO for an additional year. We reiterate our strong support for the Secretary-General and his Personal Envoy, Staffan de Mistura, in advancing the political process toward a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable solution providing for self-determination in line with the principles of the United Nations Charter. We appreciate the penholder's efforts to maintain a balanced text and stand ready to vote in favour.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea fully supports the draft resolution renewing the mandate of MINURSO for another year. We appreciate the penholder's balanced text, which appropriately emphasizes the need for a realistic, practicable, and mutually acceptable political solution based on compromise. We reiterate our steadfast support for the efforts of the Secretary-General and Personal Envoy Staffan de Mistura, as well as the essential operational role played by MINURSO on the ground.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation regrets that the penholder has once again ignored our well-founded, constructive proposals aimed at restoring balance and impartiality to the draft. By clinging to the outdated round-table format and artificially blurring the distinction between the two conflicting parties and neighbouring States, the text does not reflect realities on the ground or facilitate a mutually acceptable settlement. If the penholder proceeds with this unbalanced text without accommodating our principled concerns, the Russian Federation will be unable to support it and will abstain.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone fully supports the draft resolution as presented by the penholder. The text effectively maintains the necessary balance, renews MINURSO's critical mandate, and reaffirms the centrality of the UN-led political process aimed at achieving a realistic, practicable, and mutually acceptable solution based on compromise. We appreciate the preservation of language acknowledging the credibility of the Moroccan autonomy initiative and the round-table framework, and we look forward to voting in favour.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia appreciates the penholder's efforts to facilitate consensus on the renewal of MINURSO's mandate, which we fully support given the mission's crucial stabilizing role. As a cross-cutting matter, we continue to believe that independent human rights monitoring and unhindered access for OHCHR to both Western Sahara and the Tindouf camps are vital for building confidence and supporting a sustainable political solution. We encourage the penholder to reflect this principle in the preambular text.
messages.Somalia: Somalia fully supports the draft resolution extending the mandate of MINURSO for another year and thanks the United States for its balanced penholdership. We reaffirm our commitment to the UN-facilitated political process led by Personal Envoy Staffan de Mistura and support a realistic, pragmatic, and enduring political solution based on compromise. We also welcome constructive initiatives aimed at achieving lasting peace and stability in the region, including serious and credible efforts such as the Moroccan Autonomy Initiative.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom thanks the United States for its collaborative approach as penholder and for incorporating our language on the full, equal, and meaningful participation of women and youth in the political process. We believe this draft strikes the necessary balance, ensuring the vital continuation of MINURSO's mandate while reaffirming Council support for the Personal Envoy's efforts towards a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable political solution based on compromise. The United Kingdom fully supports the text as currently drafted and is ready to vote in favour.

steps.summary: As penholder, the United States maintained the draft resolution without changes to preserve the delicate balance established in resolution 2756. We rejected Russia's proposals to dismantle the round-table format and remove reference to Morocco's autonomy initiative, noting Russia's position to abstain rather than veto, while maintaining agreed human rights language to secure broad Council support. The draft is expected to be adopted comfortably with 13 votes in favour and 1 abstention.

Taking note of the Moroccan proposal presented on 11 April 2007 to the Secretary-General and welcoming serious and credible Moroccan efforts to move the process forward towards resolution; also taking note of the Frente POLISARIO proposal presented on 10 April 2007 to the Secretary-General,

Encouraging in this context the parties to demonstrate further political will towards a solution including by expanding upon their discussion of each other’s proposals and recommitting to UN efforts in a spirit of realism and compromise, further encouraging neighbouring countries to make contributions to the political process; and stressing the importance of all concerned expanding on their positions in order to advance a solution,

Stressing the importance of improving the human rights situation in Western Sahara and the Tindouf camps, and encouraging the parties to work actively with the international community to develop and implement independent and credible measures and to ensure full respect for human rights, bearing in mind their relevant obligations under international law, and strongly urging enhancing cooperation with the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR), including through facilitating visits to the region,

Welcoming in this regard, steps and initiatives taken by Morocco, and the role played by the National Council on Human Rights Commissions operating in Dakhla and Laayoune, and Morocco’s interaction with Special Procedures of the United Nations Human Rights Council,

Encouraging the parties to sustain and prioritize their respective efforts to enhance the promotion and protection of human rights in Western Sahara and the Tindouf refugee camps, including the freedoms of expression and association,

Noting with deep concern the continued hardships faced by Sahrawi refugees and their dependency on external humanitarian assistance, and further noting with deep concern insufficient funding for those living in Tindouf refugee camps and the risks associated with the reduction of food assistance; and strongly encouraging donors to provide additional funds in light of the deteriorating humanitarian situation and for aid agencies to facilitate the delivery of humanitarian assistance in accordance with United Nations best practices,

Strongly reiterating its request for a refugee registration in the Tindouf refugee camps and emphasizing the importance of efforts being made in this regard,

Recalling United Nations Security Council resolutions 1325 (2000) and 2250 (2015) and related resolutions; stressing the importance of a commitment by the parties to continue the process of negotiations through the United Nations-sponsored talks and encouraging the full, equal and meaningful participation of women and active and meaningful participation of youth in these talks,

Affirming its full support for Special Representative of the Secretary-General for Western Sahara and Head of MINURSO Alexander Ivanko,

Having considered the report of the Secretary-General of October 2025,

1. Decides to extend the mandate of MINURSO until 31 October 2026;

2. Emphasizes the need to achieve a realistic, practicable, enduring and mutually acceptable political solution to the question of Western Sahara based on compromise and the importance of aligning the strategic focus of MINURSO and orienting resources of the United Nations to this end;

3. Expresses its full support for the Secretary-General and his Personal Envoy to facilitate the negotiations process in order to achieve a solution to the Western Sahara question, building on the progress and framework of the former Personal Envoy, and strongly encourages Morocco, the Frente POLISARIO, Algeria, and Mauritania to engage with the Personal Envoy throughout the duration of this process, in a spirit of realism and compromise, to ensure a successful outcome;

4. Calls upon the parties to resume negotiations under the auspices of the Secretary-General without preconditions and in good faith, taking into account the efforts made since 2006, relevant Security Council resolutions, and subsequent developments with a view to achieving a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable political solution, which will provide for the self-determination of the people of Western Sahara in the context of arrangements consistent with the principles and purposes of the Charter of the United Nations, and noting the role and responsibilities of the parties in this respect;

5. Reaffirms the need for full respect of the military agreements reached with MINURSO with regard to the ceasefire and calls on the parties to comply fully with those agreements, implement their commitments, and refrain from any actions that could undermine UN-facilitated negotiations or further destabilize the situation in Western Sahara;

6. Reiterates its call upon all parties to cooperate fully with MINURSO, including its free interaction with all interlocutors, and to take the necessary steps to ensure the security of as well as unhindered movement and immediate access for the United Nations and associated personnel in carrying out their mandate, in conformity with agreements made with the United Nations;

7. Calls for the safe, regular, and unhindered resupply of MINURSO team sites to ensure the sustainability of the Mission’s presence and operations east of the berm;

8. Emphasizes the importance of a renewed commitment by the parties to advancing the political process in preparation for further negotiations, recalls that realism and a spirit of compromise by the parties are essential to achieve progress, encourages neighbouring countries to make important, active contributions to this process, and stresses the importance of all concerned expanding on their positions;

9. Calls upon the parties to demonstrate political will and work in an atmosphere propitious for dialogue in order to advance negotiations;

10. Requests the Secretary-General to brief the Security Council regularly, and at any time he deems appropriate during the mandate period, on the status and progress of these negotiations under his auspices, on the implementation of this resolution, on challenges to MINURSO’s operations, and on steps taken to address them, and to provide a report on the situation in Western Sahara well before the end of the mandate period;

11. Decides to remain seized of the matter.

reasons.China: China consistently supports the renewal of MINURSO's mandate to maintain regional stability and advance a political solution, aligning with its established voting record and position during consultations.
reasons.Denmark: Denmark consistently supports the renewal of MINURSO's mandate and the UN-led political process aimed at achieving a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable political solution providing for self-determination. In line with Council practice for members voting in favour, Denmark casts an affirmative vote without delivering a statement prior to the vote.
reasons.France: France consistently supports the renewal of MINURSO's mandate and the UN-led political process, viewing Morocco's 2007 autonomy plan as the only credible basis for a just and lasting solution, and reserves its explanation of vote for after the adoption.
reasons.Greece: Greece consistently supports the extension of MINURSO's mandate and the UN-led political process aimed at reaching a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable political solution in accordance with relevant Security Council resolutions.
reasons.Guyana: Guyana supports the extension of MINURSO's mandate to maintain stability on the ground and support the UN-led political process aimed at achieving a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable political solution that provides for the self-determination of the people of Western Sahara. In line with our affirmative vote on resolution 2756 (2024), we vote in favour of the renewal despite our preferred human rights language not being incorporated.
reasons.Pakistan: Pakistan consistently supports the mandate renewals for MINURSO and the UN-facilitated political process to achieve a just and mutually acceptable political solution providing for self-determination in accordance with UN principles.
reasons.Panama: Panama consistently supports the renewal of MINURSO's mandate and the UN-led political process aimed at achieving a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable political solution in Western Sahara.
reasons.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea consistently supports MINURSO's mandate renewal and the UN-led political process aimed at reaching a realistic, practicable, and enduring political solution. As the draft resolution aligns with previous consensus-supported texts and maintains the vital role of MINURSO, we vote in favour.
reasons.Russian Federation: Russia abstains in line with its consistent voting record on Western Sahara resolutions, as the penholder once again disregarded our principled proposals to ensure a balanced text, distinguish clearly between the parties to the conflict and neighbouring states, and eliminate outdated references to the round-table format. We choose to deliver our explanation of vote after the adoption.
reasons.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone consistently supports the renewal of MINURSO's mandate and the UN-facilitated political process, while viewing Morocco's autonomy initiative as a credible, realistic, and viable framework for resolving the dispute. In accordance with its established voting record and positive stance during consultations, Sierra Leone votes in favour of the draft resolution and will deliver any statement after the vote.
reasons.Slovenia: Slovenia consistently supports the renewal of MINURSO's mandate and the political process led by Personal Envoy De Mistura, even though our proposed language strengthening OHCHR access was not incorporated. In line with our standard practice on this agenda item, we vote in favour and will deliver any explanation of vote after the adoption.
reasons.Somalia: Somalia firmly supports the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Kingdom of Morocco, recognizes the Moroccan Autonomy Initiative as a serious and credible basis for resolving the dispute, and supports extending MINURSO's mandate to facilitate UN-led political efforts.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom consistently supports the renewal of MINURSO's mandate and the UN-led political process under the Personal Envoy, and aligns with the penholder's draft resolution while reserving any remarks for an explanation of vote following the adoption.
reasons.United States of America: As the penholder and sponsor of the draft resolution renewing MINURSO's mandate, the United States fully supports the text and votes in favour, reserving its substantive remarks for an explanation of vote after the adoption.

after.China:
China voted in favour of the resolution just adopted.

Over the years, the United Nations Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (MINURSO) has diligently fulfilled the mandate authorized by the Security Council, playing an important role in maintaining peace and stability in Western Sahara and creating conditions for advancing the political process. China commends the dedication and contributions of the Mission and its peacekeepers and supports the extension of MINURSO’s mandate.

China’s position on the question of Western Sahara is consistent and clear. We support a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable political solution reached through consultations on an equal footing among the parties concerned, on the basis of relevant Security Council resolutions. China supports the Personal Envoy of the Secretary-General, Mr. Staffan de Mistura, in his continued mediation efforts, and encourages all parties to engage in constructive dialogue in a spirit of realism and compromise to achieve progress in the political settlement.

China has consistently advocated that Security Council decisions should fully reflect the latest developments on the ground and accommodate the legitimate concerns of all relevant parties. We hope that in future discussions on the mandate of MINURSO, the penholder will carry out more comprehensive, transparent, and inclusive consultations, heed the views of all parties, and strive to build the broadest possible consensus. China stands ready to continue to play a constructive role in promoting a peaceful and proper settlement of the question of Western Sahara.
after.Denmark:
Denmark voted in favour of the resolution extending the mandate of MINURSO for another year. We thank the United States as penholder for its efforts in facilitating this outcome.

Denmark reiterates its full support for the Secretary-General and his Personal Envoy, Staffan de Mistura, in their dedicated efforts to advance the political process. We urge all parties—Morocco, the Frente POLISARIO, Algeria, and Mauritania—to re-engage in good faith, without preconditions, and in a spirit of realism and compromise, to achieve a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable political solution that provides for the self-determination of the people of Western Sahara, consistent with the principles and purposes of the Charter of the United Nations.

We remain deeply concerned about the ongoing breakdown of the ceasefire and the risk of further escalation. Denmark calls on all parties to respect their commitments, uphold the ceasefire, and avoid any actions that could undermine stability or the political process.

MINURSO plays an indispensable role in maintaining stability on the ground and supporting the United Nations' political efforts. It is imperative that the Mission is granted full, unhindered freedom of movement and safe, regular access to resupply all its team sites east and west of the berm.

Finally, Denmark attaches the utmost importance to the promotion and protection of human rights. We call for strengthened cooperation by all parties with the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights, including by facilitating visits to Western Sahara and the refugee camps in Tindouf. We also remain concerned by the difficult humanitarian conditions faced by the Sahrawi refugees and emphasize the need for sustained donor support and the facilitation of humanitarian assistance in line with United Nations standards.
after.France:
France welcomes the adoption of the resolution renewing the mandate of the United Nations Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (MINURSO) for another year.

Thanks to this decision, MINURSO will be able to continue fulfilling its essential role in maintaining regional stability and facilitating the political process. We commend the Mission’s personnel, under the leadership of Special Representative Alexander Ivanko, for their dedication under challenging conditions. It remains vital that MINURSO enjoys full freedom of movement and that the safe and regular resupply of its team sites, particularly east of the sand wall, is fully guaranteed.

France reiterates its full support for the Personal Envoy of the Secretary-General, Mr. Staffan de Mistura. We encourage all parties—Morocco, the Frente POLISARIO, Algeria, and Mauritania—to re-engage in good faith, in a spirit of realism and compromise, and to resume the round-table process without preconditions in order to achieve a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable political solution in line with relevant Security Council resolutions.

We remain deeply concerned by the continued breakdown of the ceasefire and the low-intensity hostilities that jeopardize regional stability. France calls for a complete cessation of hostilities and a return to the full observance of the ceasefire.

France’s position on this issue is clear, historic, and constant. For France, the present and future of Western Sahara lie within the framework of Moroccan sovereignty. Autonomy under Moroccan sovereignty is the only basis for achieving a just, lasting, and negotiated political solution to this dispute. The autonomy plan presented by Morocco in 2007 represents a serious, credible, and realistic basis to move the political process forward, and there is now an undeniable international consensus emerging around it. France remains committed to accompanying all efforts towards stability, cooperation, and development for the benefit of the populations of the region.
after.Greece:
Greece voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, which extends the mandate of the United Nations Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (MINURSO) for another year.

Greece reaffirms its full and steadfast support for the United Nations-led political process and for the tireless efforts of the Secretary-General and his Personal Envoy, Mr. Staffan de Mistura. We encourage all parties—Morocco, the Frente POLISARIO, Algeria, and Mauritania—to re-engage in good faith, without preconditions, and in a spirit of realism and compromise, in order to achieve a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable political solution in accordance with the relevant Security Council resolutions and the principles and purposes of the Charter of the United Nations. In this regard, we take note of serious and credible efforts to advance the process towards a viable resolution.

We also express our full confidence in and appreciation for MINURSO and the Special Representative of the Secretary-General, Mr. Alexander Ivanko. MINURSO plays an indispensable stabilizing role on the ground, and it is vital that the Mission is granted full, safe, and unhindered freedom of movement and regular access to resupply its team sites so that it can discharge its mandate effectively.

As a Mediterranean nation, Greece attaches the utmost importance to peace, security, and stability across North Africa and the wider region. We call on all parties to respect the ceasefire, refrain from any acts that could escalate tensions, and work constructively towards regional cooperation and a peaceful, enduring settlement.
after.Guyana:
Mr. President,

Guyana voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, which extends the mandate of the United Nations Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (MINURSO) for an additional year.

Our support for this resolution reflects Guyana’s steadfast commitment to the maintenance of international peace and security and our conviction that MINURSO plays an indispensable role in stabilizing the situation on the ground, monitoring the ceasefire, and creating the necessary conditions to facilitate a peaceful political process. We reiterate our full support for the Special Representative of the Secretary-General, Mr. Alexander Ivanko, and the dedicated personnel of MINURSO, who continue to carry out their mandate under challenging circumstances.

At the same time, Guyana reaffirms its principled and unwavering support for the right of the people of Western Sahara to self-determination, in accordance with the Charter of the United Nations and relevant General Assembly and Security Council resolutions. We continue to advocate for a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable political solution that provides for the self-determination of the people of Western Sahara.

In this regard, we express our full confidence in and support for the Personal Envoy of the Secretary-General, Mr. Staffan de Mistura. We encourage all parties—Morocco and the Frente POLISARIO—as well as neighbouring States, to engage constructively, in good faith, and without preconditions, in UN-led negotiations and consultations to advance the political process.

Guyana also emphasizes the vital importance of human rights in the resolution of this conflict. We remain convinced that independent, credible, and comprehensive human rights monitoring throughout Western Sahara and in the refugee camps in Tindouf is essential. We encourage enhanced cooperation with the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) and urge that unhindered access be granted to human rights bodies and mandate holders.

Finally, we call upon the parties to fully respect the ceasefire, refrain from unilateral actions that could escalate tensions, and demonstrate the necessary political will to achieve a peaceful and enduring solution.

I thank you.
after.Pakistan:
Pakistan voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, extending the mandate of the United Nations Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (MINURSO) for another year.

Pakistan attaches great importance to the peaceful and early resolution of the question of Western Sahara, involving as it does countries with which Pakistan enjoys close, fraternal, and brotherly relations. 

Our vote today reflects our consistent support for the efforts of the United Nations to reach a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable political solution to this long-standing dispute. Central to this process is the fundamental principle of the self-determination of peoples, which is enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations and reaffirmed in relevant resolutions of the Security Council. Pakistan has consistently maintained that all resolutions of the Security Council must be implemented in letter and spirit.

We reiterate our full support for the Secretary-General and his Personal Envoy, Mr. Staffan de Mistura, and welcome his persistent engagement to advance the political process. We encourage all parties to engage constructively, in good faith and without preconditions, in a spirit of realism and compromise, to resume dialogue and achieve tangible progress. 

As a major troop-contributing country that remains deeply committed to UN peacekeeping, Pakistan also commends the dedicated women and men of MINURSO for their service under challenging circumstances. We urge all parties to extend full cooperation to MINURSO, ensuring the safety, security, and unhindered movement of its personnel so that the Mission can effectively fulfill its mandate.

Pakistan will continue to support all constructive efforts aimed at fostering dialogue, peace, and stability in the region.

I thank you, Madam President.
after.Russian Federation:
The Russian Federation abstained in the voting on the draft resolution prepared by the United States on the extension of the mandate of the United Nations Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (MINURSO).

Our principled position on the settlement of the Western Sahara issue remains consistent and unchanged. We have consistently advocated for a balanced, objective, and unbiased approach that would facilitate a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable solution to the problem of Western Sahara, in strict accordance with the Charter of the United Nations and relevant Security Council resolutions, providing for the self-determination of the people of Western Sahara.

Unfortunately, our constructive and well-substantiated comments, which we have repeatedly conveyed to the American penholders year after year, were once again disregarded. The text adopted today does not reflect the reality on the ground and fails to take into account the concerns of all interested sides. We regret that the resolution continues to reproduce unbalanced formulations that predetermine the parameters of the political process rather than foster an environment conducive to direct and unconditional dialogue.

In particular, we continue to question the persistent inclusion of references to the round-table format, which has long lost its relevance, has reached an impasse, and only constrains the mediation efforts of the Personal Envoy of the Secretary-General, Mr. Staffan de Mistura. We also cannot agree with attempts to blur the clear distinction between the actual parties to the conflict—namely, Morocco and the Frente POLISARIO—and the neighboring States.

At the same time, we wish to underscore our full support for the work of MINURSO as a key stabilizing presence on the ground, as well as for the mediation efforts of the Personal Envoy of the Secretary-General. We urge the parties to refrain from unilateral steps and escalation, and to demonstrate genuine political will to resume direct negotiations without preconditions, in order to achieve a viable and mutually acceptable political solution.
after.Sierra Leone:
Sierra Leone welcomes the adoption of the resolution renewing the mandate of the United Nations Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (MINURSO) for a period of one year. We commend the United States, as the penholder, for its constructive engagement and stewardship throughout the negotiation process, as well as all Council members for their collaborative approach.

Sierra Leone voted in favour of the resolution, consistent with our unwavering commitment to peace, stability, and security in the region. MINURSO continues to play an indispensable role on the ground in maintaining calm, monitoring the ceasefire, and creating an environment conducive to advancing the political process. We emphasize the necessity of ensuring the safety, security, and unhindered movement of MINURSO personnel, as well as the regular and safe resupply of its team sites.

My delegation reaffirms its full support for the United Nations-led political process under the auspices of the Secretary-General, and we commend the dedicated efforts of his Personal Envoy, Mr. Staffan de Mistura, to revitalize negotiations. We urge all concerned parties—Morocco, the Frente POLISARIO, Algeria, and Mauritania—to engage in good faith and without preconditions in the round-table process, building on the progress achieved, and to demonstrate the requisite political will in a spirit of realism and compromise to achieve a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable political solution.

In this context, Sierra Leone reiterates its strong support for the Moroccan Autonomy Initiative presented in 2007, which represents a credible, realistic, and pragmatic basis for resolving this protracted dispute, consistent with international law and relevant Security Council resolutions. We also note with appreciation the socioeconomic development initiatives undertaken by Morocco in the region, as well as its constructive engagement with international human rights mechanisms and the National Human Rights Commission.

In conclusion, Sierra Leone calls on all stakeholders to refrain from any actions that could escalate tensions or undermine the political process. Only through constructive dialogue, trust-building, and compromise can we achieve an enduring resolution that brings peace, stability, and prosperity to the peoples of the Maghreb and Sahel regions.

I thank you.
after.Slovenia:
Slovenia welcomes the adoption of the resolution extending the mandate of the United Nations Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (MINURSO). We voted in favour of this resolution, reaffirming our steadfast support for the vital work of the Mission, which plays an indispensable role in maintaining stability on the ground.

Slovenia reiterates its full commitment to achieving a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable political solution that provides for the self-determination of the people of Western Sahara, in accordance with the principles and purposes of the Charter of the United Nations and relevant Security Council resolutions. 

We express our full support for the Personal Envoy of the Secretary-General, Staffan de Mistura, and his tireless efforts to advance the political process. We urge all parties to engage constructively, in good faith, without preconditions, and in a spirit of compromise. We also commend Special Representative Alexander Ivanko and the military and civilian personnel of MINURSO for their dedication under challenging conditions.

Furthermore, Slovenia continues to emphasize the critical importance of human rights. We believe that human rights monitoring and reporting strengthen United Nations peace operations and contribute to sustainable peace. In this regard, we reiterate our call for unhindered and meaningful access for the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) throughout the territory and to the Tindouf refugee camps. We also remain concerned by the difficult humanitarian conditions faced by the refugees and urge the international community to maintain adequate support.

Finally, we call upon all parties to fully respect the ceasefire, refrain from unilateral actions, and cooperate fully with MINURSO to ensure its safe and regular operations.
after.Somalia:
Mr. President,

Somalia voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, which extends the mandate of the United Nations Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (MINURSO) for another year. We thank the United States, as the penholder, for its efforts in facilitating this text.

Somalia reaffirms its steadfast support for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Kingdom of Morocco over its entire national territory, including the Moroccan Sahara. In this regard, we commend Morocco’s serious and credible efforts, particularly the Autonomy Initiative presented in 2007, which provides a realistic, practical, and enduring basis for achieving a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable political solution to this long-standing regional dispute.

My delegation reiterates its full support for the Secretary-General and his Personal Envoy, Mr. Staffan de Mistura, in their dedicated efforts to facilitate the political process. We urge the resumption of the round-table consultations with the constructive engagement of all four participants—Morocco, the Frente POLISARIO, Algeria, and Mauritania—in a spirit of realism and compromise, without preconditions and in good faith.

Finally, Somalia pays tribute to the men and women serving in MINURSO. We underscore the essential role the Mission plays in monitoring the ceasefire and maintaining stability in the region, and we call for the full respect of its mandate, including ensuring the safety, security, and unhindered freedom of movement of its personnel.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
The United Kingdom welcomes the adoption of this resolution, which renews the mandate of the United Nations Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (MINURSO) for a further 12 months.

The United Kingdom has consistently supported MINURSO, and we express our deep appreciation to Special Representative Alexander Ivanko and the military and civilian personnel of the Mission for their dedication and vital work under often challenging conditions. We urge all parties to ensure MINURSO’s safe, unhindered access and the regular resupply of its team sites across the territory.

We also thank the United States, as penholder, for its efforts in facilitating discussions and presenting a balanced text that supports the Mission and the broader political process.

The United Kingdom reaffirms its full support for the Personal Envoy of the Secretary-General, Staffan de Mistura, and his tireless efforts to advance the political process. We urge the parties—Morocco and the Frente POLISARIO—as well as neighbouring States, Algeria and Mauritania, to engage constructively, without preconditions and in a spirit of realism and compromise, to resume consultations and move towards a political solution. 

The United Kingdom remains firmly committed to assisting the parties to achieve a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable political solution based on compromise, which will provide for the self-determination of the people of Western Sahara in the context of arrangements consistent with the principles and purposes of the Charter of the United Nations.

We remain concerned by the continued breakdown of the ceasefire and reiterate our call on the parties to respect their military agreements and avoid any actions that could escalate tensions. Furthermore, the United Kingdom emphasizes the importance of human rights monitoring and encourages enhanced cooperation with the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights, including by facilitating visits to the region. 

We look forward to continued close cooperation with all Council members, the Secretariat, and regional partners to achieve lasting peace and stability for the people of Western Sahara and the wider region.
after.United States of America:
The United States is pleased to see the Security Council reaffirm its support for the Personal Envoy of the Secretary-General, Mr. Staffan de Mistura, and for the United Nations Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (MINURSO), led by Special Representative Alexander Ivanko, with the adoption of this resolution renewing MINURSO’s mandate for another year.

Today, the Council has sent a clear and unequivocal message that we must urgently intensify efforts to achieve a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable political solution without further delay. We appreciate the constructive engagement of Council members throughout the negotiations on this text. While we welcome the broad and overwhelming support for this resolution, we regret that the Council was once again unable to achieve unanimity, as unity sends the strongest possible signal of international resolve in support of peace.

The United States strongly supports Personal Envoy de Mistura in his efforts to advance the political process. It is vital that all parties—Morocco, the Frente POLISARIO, Algeria, and Mauritania—engage with the Personal Envoy in good faith, without preconditions, and in a spirit of realism and compromise, building upon the framework and progress of previous discussions, including the resumption of the round-table format.

A durable political solution is essential to ensuring a peaceful, secure, and prosperous future for the people of Western Sahara and the wider region. In this regard, the United States continues to view Morocco’s autonomy proposal as serious, credible, and realistic, and a potential approach to satisfy the aspirations of the people of Western Sahara.

By adopting this resolution, the Council has also reaffirmed the indispensable role played by MINURSO on the ground. To carry out its vital mandate, MINURSO must be granted full freedom of movement and safe, unimpeded, and regular access to resupply its team sites. We urge the full respect for ceasefire agreements and the cessation of hostilities to prevent further escalation and to foster an environment conducive to political dialogue. Furthermore, we emphasize the urgent need to address the humanitarian needs and human rights of Sahrawi refugees in the Tindouf camps, including through enhanced support from international donors.

The United States remains committed to working with Council members and regional partners to support the Personal Envoy’s efforts to bring an enduring and dignified resolution to this long-standing conflict.
